title: PM2.5
summary: Fine particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or smaller.
why_it_matters: Because these particles are very small, they can travel deep into the lungs and are commonly used in public air-quality messaging.
how_to_read: Lower values are generally better. Sustained spikes usually indicate dust, combustion, traffic, or other particulate events.

title: PM10
summary: Coarser particulate matter up to 10 micrometres in diameter.
why_it_matters: PM10 is useful for understanding dust-heavy conditions, including regional dust storms and coarse suspended particles.
how_to_read: PM10 can rise sharply during wind-driven dust events. Compare it with PM2.5 to understand how coarse or fine the particulate load is.

title: CO₂
summary: Carbon dioxide concentration measured in parts per million.
why_it_matters: CO₂ is commonly used as a ventilation and occupancy proxy, especially for indoor or near-building deployments.
how_to_read: Treat CO₂ as a context signal rather than a general outdoor pollution score.

title: Relative Humidity
summary: The amount of water vapour in the air relative to the maximum it can hold at that temperature.
why_it_matters: Humidity affects comfort, sensor interpretation, haze, and the apparent feel of outdoor conditions.
how_to_read: Humidity is most useful when read together with temperature and precipitation.

title: Atmospheric Pressure
summary: The pressure exerted by the atmosphere on the sensor location.
why_it_matters: Pressure helps interpret weather changes and supports quality-control checks for meteorological stations.
how_to_read: Pressure trends are usually more informative than a single reading.

title: Temperature
summary: Air temperature measured at the station.
why_it_matters: Temperature helps contextualize heat events, comfort, and the behaviour of other signals such as humidity and ozone.
how_to_read: Look for persistent daytime peaks, nighttime recovery, and sudden anomalies during heat events.

title: Air Quality Index
summary: A public-facing interpretation layer that converts pollutant concentrations into easier-to-read categories.
why_it_matters: AQI helps general audiences quickly understand whether conditions are good, moderate, or unhealthy.
how_to_read: This redesign uses AQI-style contextual bands for particulate matter so that charts communicate meaning, not just numbers.

title: Dust Storm Event
summary: A marker used to flag a likely dust-driven particulate spike or wind-driven event in the time-series view.
why_it_matters: Event markers help users connect sudden changes in particulate matter to real-world environmental conditions.
how_to_read: Markers are heuristically detected from recent data and can be supplemented with manual or forecast-based events later.
